penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: An agent orchestration layer that actually works for diverse solo SaaS operators requires per-customer setup, workflow customization, and debugging — each customer's stack is different, demanding hands-on configuration work that Claude alone cannot generalize away.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: When agents fail or produce unexpected outputs, solo founders escalate urgently; support requires human judgement about their specific codebase and context.

rationale: Solo SaaS founders genuinely suffer from the gap between LLM marketing and practical agent operation, and they already pay for AI tooling — so the pain and buyer clarity are real. However, building a genuinely useful agent orchestration layer is a hard engineering product (it's what companies like Linear, Cursor, and Vercel are building with large teams), and the delivery model is inherently high-touch: each customer's backlog, tech stack, and acceptable risk tolerance differs, meaning per-customer manual setup and support are unavoidable. Operational autonomy scores very low because the factory cannot autonomously customize an agent pipeline for an unknown SaaS product — this would be consulting, not a productized micro-service. The penalties bring the total below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: Not realistically buildable as a solo, hands-off micro-service. What a solo operator could offer is a templated 'agent task queue' document system — a Claude-powered Notion/Markdown workflow where customers paste their backlog and Claude breaks it into agent-executable subtasks with cost estimates. BUILD: factory builds a form intake + Claude prompt pipeline + a PDF/Markdown output + Stripe payment link. SELL: reach solo SaaS founders via Indie Hackers, HN, and X/Twitter; outreach approved by operator. MAINTAIN: delivery is automated (Claude processes intake, emails output), billing via Stripe. BUT: this is a one-time document product, not recurring SaaS — and it doesn't solve the actual orchestration problem the buyer wants. A solo non-technical operator cannot build a true agent orchestration platform; be honest that the simplified version (a planning document) is far weaker than what buyers need.
notes: Total 3.6 falls below min_total_to_validate (5.5) — recommended drop. operational_autonomy gate also unmet (score 4, floor 7).
